patterns.resolution: Fix bootargs: remove space in 'ttyS0, 115200' -> 'ttyS0,115200'. Ensure enable_uart=1 in /boot/config.txt and correct pinctrl state in device tree.
Check bootargs for typos or misplaced spaces. Common mistake: 'console=ttyS0, 115200' should be 'console=ttyS0,115200' (no space after comma).

patterns.match: card did not respond to voltage select
patterns.resolution: 1) Reseat the SD card. 2) Try a different SD card. 3) Check power supply (must be 5V/2.5A minimum for RPi 3B+). 4) Check for oxidized contacts.

The kernel encountered an unrecoverable error. Check the lines above for the root cause (NULL deref, OOM, init killed). If 'VFS: Unable to mount root fs', verify root= in bootargs points to correct partition.
A kernel driver accessed invalid memory. Check the Call Trace for the faulting module. If it's a third-party driver, try updating the kernel. If in a core module, file a bug report.
System ran out of RAM. 1) Reduce running services. 2) Add swap space: 'sudo dphys-swapfile setup && sudo dphys-swapfile swapon'. 3) Check for memory leaks in applications.
A kernel assertion failed. Check the file:line reference (e.g., net/core/skbuff.c:102). Update to the latest kernel with 'sudo rpi-update'. If persistent, report to raspberrypi/linux.
A CPU got stuck in a long-running kernel operation. Often caused by: 1) SD card I/O delays. 2) Buggy kernel module. 3) Hardware overheating. Check 'vcgencmd measure_temp'.
The ext4 filesystem detected errors. 1) Run 'fsck.ext4 -f /dev/mmcblk0p2' from another system. 2) Check SD card health with 'badblocks'. 3) Replace SD card if errors persist.
Physical read/write failure on SD card. 1) Backup data immediately. 2) Re-image the SD card. 3) Use a high-quality A2-rated card. 4) Check power supply stability.
The SD host controller timed out. 1) Try a slower SD card clock: add 'dtparam=sd_overclock=25' in /boot/config.txt. 2) Check for loose SD card connection.
Kernel cannot find the root partition. 1) Verify 'root=/dev/mmcblk0p2' in bootargs. 2) Check partition table with fdisk. 3) Ensure the filesystem is not corrupted.
The init system (PID 1) crashed. 1) Boot into recovery: add 'init=/bin/sh' to bootargs. 2) Check /sbin/init exists and is executable. 3) Re-install systemd: 'apt install --reinstall systemd'.
Ethernet PHY did not initialize. 1) Check if Ethernet cable is plugged in. 2) For USB Ethernet (RPi 3B+), ensure USB hub enumerates. 3) Try 'dtoverlay=lan78xx' in config.txt.
U-Boot's EFI boot manager failed. 1) Set manual boot: 'setenv bootcmd "fatload mmc 0:1 ${kernel_addr_r} kernel8.img; booti ..."'. 2) Ensure kernel8.img exists on SD card.

patterns.match: fdt and atags support not compiled in
patterns.resolution: The kernel was booted without a device tree blob. Pass the DTB: 'fatload mmc 0:1 ${fdt_addr_r} bcm2710-rpi-3-b-plus.dtb' before calling booti.
U-Boot cannot find its saved environment file. Run 'saveenv' in U-Boot console to create it. This is normal on first boot with a new SD card.
A USB device failed to enumerate. 1) Unplug and replug the device. 2) Try a powered USB hub. 3) Check power supply. 4) Add 'max_usb_current=1' to config.txt.
A userspace process crashed. Check the process name and address. 1) Reinstall the affected package. 2) Check for SD card corruption. 3) Test RAM with memtester.
CPU is overheating and throttling. 1) Add a heatsink and fan. 2) Reduce CPU load. 3) Check ambient temperature. 4) Set 'arm_freq=1200' in config.txt to reduce heat.

patterns.match: no bootable image found|cannot load any image
patterns.resolution: U-Boot cannot find a bootable kernel image. 1) Check SD card has kernel8.img (RPi 4) or kernel7.img (RPi 3). 2) Verify FAT partition is intact: 'fsck.vfat /dev/mmcblk0p1'. 3) Re-flash the SD card with Raspberry Pi Imager.
Kernel bootargs are not set. In U-Boot console: 'setenv bootargs "console=ttyS0,115200 root=/dev/mmcblk0p2 rootwait rw"' then 'saveenv'. Or add them to boot.scr / extlinux.conf.
The system triggered a full reset. This usually means a fatal error in U-Boot. Check the lines above for the root cause (missing FDT, bootargs, or kernel image).
Network boot (PXE/BOOTP) was attempted but no DHCP server responded. If not using network boot, set 'setenv boot_targets mmc0' in U-Boot to skip network boot.
Excessive backspace characters detected in the U-Boot console, indicating manual typing. This suggests the operator was debugging interactively. Check if bootcmd is set correctly for autonomous boot.
